messages:
sam: Heads-up — onboarding sample app hit inconsistent error shapes when token refresh fails. Node vs Python behave very differently, breaking our sample app tests.
elaine: Can you paste the minimal repro or a snippet?
sam: repro attached below (trimmed):
```js
// node sdk
try { await client.generate(...) } catch (e) { console.log(e) }
// logs: { error: { type: 'AuthError', message: 'token expired', status: 401 } }
```
```py
# python sdk
try:
    client.generate(...)
except Exception as e:
    print(repr(e))
# logs: RedwoodAuthError('token invalid')  # no status, no hint attr
```
sam: Node surfaces status and nested object, python raises a single opaque exception with no structured fields. Very frustrating for sample apps that programmatically retry/inspect.
mike: Oof. We had a parity agreement to expose typed exceptions with: code (string enum), status (int), message, retry_hint (nullable string). Why is python losing structured attrs?
nora: I think python wrapper wraps and only preserves message. Also streaming frames return plain text errors (non-JSON) sometimes which makes parsing brittle.
elaine: We should draft a minimal error contract doc + spec that SDKs can implement. Suggest canonical fields: { code, status, message, retryable, retry_hint, request_id } and for 429 include retry_after header when available.
mike: +1. Also include a human-facing message and machine code separate fields so apps can show something friendly without parsing code.
sam: Example canonical shape I'm proposing: 
```json
{
  "code": "AUTH_EXPIRED",
  "status": 401,
  "message": "Access token expired",
  "retryable": true,
  "retry_hint": "refresh_token",
  "request_id": "r_abc123"
}
```
elaine: Nice. SDKs should then map to typed exceptions like AuthExpiredError(status=401, retryable=True, retry_hint="refresh_token", request_id="...").
nora: For streaming clients: ensure error frames follow same JSON envelope so clients can consistently handle mid-stream failures.
mike: Implementation plan: add small ErrorCanonicalizer in runtime that returns canonical JSON on failures; SDKs call runtime endpoint and map to typed errors. I'll prototype a thin layer in node + python.
elaine: I'll update onboarding sample app to assert on canonical fields and add a short troubleshooting section: "how to detect and retry auth issues" with examples for Node and Python.
sam: Also propose adding a short SDK utility, e.g., is_retryable(err) and extract_retry_after(err) helpers.
nora: Tests: unit tests for parity + e2e using the sample app. We'll add a lint rule to flag any SDK error wrappers that swallow attrs.
deploy-bot: deploy: canary rollout queued for runtime change (job 4231).
mike: I opened WIP PR to runtime canonicalizer: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/812 — includes mapping table for common errors.
elaine: I'll own docs + sample app patch. PR incoming by Thu.
sam: Can we set an owner & a target date? My ask: EOW for docs + sample app; runtime + SDK patches can be next sprint but prototype sooner.
nora: I can cover tests and SDK test harness. Owner: @elaine docs/sample, @mike runtime + node sdk, @sam validate sample app, @nora tests. Target: docs/sample by EOW (Fri), runtime prototype by next Wed.
mike: Sounds good. I'll post an update in this thread when the node/python wrappers start preserving fields.
sam: Thanks — this will dramatically reduce onboarding friction and flaky sample app tests. :thumbsup:
elaine: Filing a short RFC doc and linking to repo patches in PRs.
mike: Also reminder: ensure 429 returns Retry-After header for clients that don't support the retry_hint field.
sam: Agreed. Also add a small note in the quickstart about how to detect "permanent" vs "transient" errors.
elaine: will do.
